name: Daffodil DB
tagline: Pure-Java SQL database from India's Daffodil Software, with an open-source edition called One$DB; abandoned.
description: Daffodil DB was a relational database written entirely in Java by Daffodil Software, an Indian software company, that could run embedded inside a Java application or as a network server. It aimed at standards compliance, with JDBC and ODBC access, a broad SQL-99 feature set and MVCC, and competed with Derby, HSQLDB and other Java engines of the mid-2000s. Alongside the commercial product the company published an open-source edition, One$DB, on SourceForge; its last files, version 4.1, date from 2006. Development stopped by the early 2010s and Daffodil Software, which still operates as a software services firm, no longer sells or supports it. Java projects today should use H2, HSQLDB, Derby or SQLite instead.
statusNote: Abandoned; the last open-source One$DB files (4.1) date from 2006 and the vendor no longer sells or supports it.

license.name: GNU LGPL v2 (One$DB edition); commercial edition proprietary

pricing.notes: No longer sold; One$DB files remain on SourceForge.

strengths: Pure Java, so it ran anywhere a JVM did, embedded or as a server
Standards-oriented SQL with JDBC and ODBC access
Open-source One$DB edition alongside the commercial product
weaknesses: Abandoned for well over a decade
Small community; documentation survives only in archives
useCases: Maintaining legacy Java applications that embed it
Historical comparison of 2000s-era Java SQL engines
notIdealFor: Anything needing support or security fixes
